page: Microsoft Azure L4ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine within the Lpsv5 family, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built on 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) and provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs alongside 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware profile does not include graphics processing units.

Storage configurations for the L4ps_v5 include a directly attached 960 GB NVMe solid-state drive for low-latency local data access, and the instance is capable of supporting Azure Premium Storage. The server does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Operating on an ARM-based compute layer, the L4ps_v5 delivers high resource density with an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with high-speed local NVMe capacity. This balance offers favorable compute-to-storage cost efficiency for input-output demanding deployments compared to standard general-purpose profiles. However, software stacks must be compatible with the arm64 instruction set architecture, and workloads relying on x86-specific instruction sets cannot run natively. Suitable applications include relational and non-relational database engines, transactional caching tiers, log indexing systems, and data processing tasks requiring fast intermediate scratch space.
description: The Microsoft Azure L4ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine from the Lpsv5 series running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an arm64 processor architecture, it features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The instance includes a bundled 960 GB local NVMe solid-state drive and supports Premium Storage, delivering fast local storage capabilities for throughput-dependent applications. No hardware GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. By combining dedicated ARM cores, generous memory density, and local high-speed NVMe storage, the L4ps_v5 offers cost-efficient operating parameters for workloads requiring consistent I/O access and substantial memory capacity. Tradeoffs include the requirement for ARM-compatible binaries and lack of x86 vector extensions. This server is structured for database hosting, in-memory caching with persistence, log aggregation, and data processing workloads requiring localized high-speed disk access.
